about: A recorded onboarding conversation and its tool calls, synthetic throughout (#1108, joined to install in #636). Steps name the install skill's onboarding road (#1358). Tool steps run the packaged helper against recording fakes; plan steps build the synthetic GitHub the fake gh answers from; the setup step stands for install's verified setup and openwiz init, whose state the helper carries forward. Nothing here is a prewritten plan: the spec and tickets come from this conversation's grill answers.

options.label: as reported by CloudRoom; it may answer from a saved copy

turns.agent: OpenWiz is a factory of coding agents: they turn one thing you want into small tickets, build each one, review each other's work and merge it.
Your agents need a place to run: this machine, or Cloudroom or another cloud host to run many at once. Cloudroom uses your Cloud Credits. Which would you like?

Three ways to start: a small change in a repository you have, a fresh project from your idea, or something you have always wanted. Ideas: a pocket weather haiku tool, a one-page fan site for your favourite synthetic band, or a tiny terminal game where you herd sheep. It goes in a new private repository, synthetic-owner/synthetic-sheep, or one of yours. Which?

turns.user: The sheep game, in a new repository.

turns.agent: This creates one private GitHub repository, synthetic-owner/synthetic-sheep, with your gh identity, with one initial commit on its default branch: a README.md holding only the title. Create it?
Created and read back. Please make a CloudRoom project for it, or pick one; setup then selects it.

Setup is next, for synthetic-owner/synthetic-sheep: sign in to GitHub in your browser, then create your own OpenWiz App or skip it, prepare the project with your harness, model and effort, and make its private brain. Each effect is shown first.

turns.user: Skip the App; act as me. Codex, syn-codex-model-01, high.

turns.agent: Setup is verified. Acting identity: synthetic-owner, your personal GitHub login (the App is skipped). The private brain is in synthetic-owner/synthetic-sheep.

Q1: Smallest fun version: one field, three sheep, arrow keys move the dog (recommended), or levels too? Q2: Scoring by time to pen all sheep (recommended) or by moves? Q3: A title screen with the best time (recommended), or none?

turns.user: One field, time scoring, yes to the title screen.

turns.agent: Summary: a terminal sheep-herding game with one field, three sheep, arrow-key dog, time scoring and a title screen. If it matches what you want, say yes here.

turns.agent: Ready: one fleet thread (codex, syn-codex-model-01, high) whose loop checks spec #900 every 10 minutes and starts 3 builders for S1, S2 and S3, each reviewed by claude-code from the other family. Start the fleet in Cloudroom now? It can cost money: it uses your Cloud Credits, unknown until measured, and model-provider charges are separate.
The plan passed its checks, so the fleet started: 3 builders, each on one small ticket. Watch them work at openwiz.dev/app; nothing for you to do until the first merge.
Three builders are working on S1 to S3; S4 and S5 wait for their blockers.
